glosses: Procéder à la rétro-ingénierie de quelque chose.

examples.text: L’un des axes principaux de recherche du PP, l’axe SETAV (Search for Extra-Terrestrial Artefact and Visitation ou Recherche d’Artefacts et de Sondes Extraterrestres), serait de découvrir, d’analyser et de rétroingéniérer les artefacts anachroniques, technologiques ou autres, potentiellement présents sur Terre : Dans le sous-sol, dans les mers et océans et au sein de l’atmosphère terrestre (sondes).
Ils ont galéré vu qu’ils ont dû rétroingéniérer le truc. (rétroingéniéré corrigé en rétroingéniérer)
Sinon, le lossless made in Apple, bien que propriétaire, est assez simple et a été "rétroingéniéré".
D’un autre côté, une applet Java peut être rétroingéniérée sans trop de problèmes, mais cacher son code n’est pas souvent une priorité absolue.
C’est assez facile à rétroingéniérer - pour une puissance donnée, on a tant de carac, tant de défense, etc. mais ça pourrait être bien de filer les templates.

Les auteurices veulent raconter une histoire donnée qu’ils ont fixé, et ils adaptent l’univers pour que l’histoire soit racontable. Si c’est fait sans que les coutures soient visibles et proprement rétroingéniéré ok, mais là c’est pas le cas du tout.
Les autres "drones" sont-ils précisément des copies rétroingéniérées à minima sur modèle BigB ?

glosses: To reverse-engineer; to analyze (an existing item) in order to determine how to replicate it.

examples.text: On other occasions, where the technical basis for the initial entry cannot be defended, the second mover has the advantage, since it may well be less costly to retro-engineer a product than to have invented and innovated it.
I suspected that's why I could so easily retro-engineer and re-invent their ultra-superior and advanced technology.

You can retro-engineer it. You look at a roomful of junk and you pay attention to what's lying on what, because that will eventually tell you what fell first.

If you can retro-engineer Sauron's ring, it isn't as magical anymore. It's a matter of the characters getting control of the material, as opposed to being in a situation or universe where this is not really possible.

glosses: To develop (a process) by starting with the goal and working backwards to determine the steps needed to achieve it.

examples.text: Use the functional interaction with your best performers to retro-engineer a mission, values, and culture check-in.

Set out the ambitions within a realistic time-frame, and re-engineer what you need to achieve in order to get there, taking into account possible interdependencies between different communication elements. This is altogether not very different from any IT project: define your goals, break it into smaller pieces, work out the interdependencies, and retro-engineer the goals into how you're going to get there.
As we noted in the previous chapter, the best method for scheduling your time is to retro-engineer—that is, work backward.

glosses: To revise or adapt (an existing item or process) in order to achieve a new purpose.

examples.text: All of this makes some sense in terms of using the windfall brownfield site to retro-engineer a more mixed use form of development, but it does show up the shortcomings of the previous approach and the difficulties of achieving the new constraint policy.
